adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration loops through `records.each do |h|` where `h` comes from the `site_settings` table value (the old `embeddable_hosts` setting), and builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any stored host line contains a single quote or other SQL-significant characters, the SQL will break (at minimum) and could potentially be exploited in a compromised DB scenario. Rails migrations should use `quote(h)` / `connection.quote(h)` or insert via AR to avoid this.
